summary: Enterprise Suite governance foundation for shared HR/Payroll/Accounting policy admission, group close projection, and metadata-only ops command envelopes.

findings: The slice implements only the suite invariants already named in specs/microservices/enterprise-suite.json AC-01..AC-03.
The domain functions are pure and boring: validate identifiers, refuse policy bypass, and project per-legal-entity close state without storage or dispatch side effects.
Suite-level policy admission prevents child services from silently diverging on tenant, legal entity, data-class, and audit evidence requirements.
Group close rollup keeps each legal entity independent and exposes only projection metadata for dashboards, preserving blast-radius boundaries for multi-entity tenants.

F3_adversarial.failing_fixture_id: policy bypass, missing payload data class, cross-tenant rollup, and manual SSH route refusal tests
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if child writes bypass the suite gateway, omit data-class evidence, mix tenant boundaries, or route day-2 operations through manual SSH.
findings: Positive and negative fixtures cover the three implemented Enterprise Suite acceptance criteria.
Identifier validation rejects prefix-only, traversal-like, and whitespace-bearing refs through shared validation helpers.
The public API exposes one admission function, one rollup function, and one app-envelope function with direct input/output structs.
Tests are named to match enterprise-suite spec acceptance criteria, making future runtime adapter work easy to map back to the machine-readable PRD.
cargo fmt, locked tests, locked clippy, catalog prefix/SLO/claim gates, cohesion, and cargo deny all passed locally.
The only new dependency is the existing in-workspace data-boundary kernel used by prior enterprise domain/app crates.

alternatives_named: defer suite shell until REST/runtime adapters exist
place suite logic inside HR, Payroll, or Accounting child crates
create pure suite domain/app crates now
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Pure suite domain/app crates satisfy existing Enterprise Suite AC-01..AC-03 without coupling child services or claiming runtime behavior.
rejected_reasons: Deferring would leave the suite-level policy gateway only as documentation while child foundations grow.
Placing suite admission inside a child crate would invert ownership and let one child become the suite boundary.

findings: Child writes must carry tenant_id, legal_entity_id, payload data class, audit evidence, idempotency key, and a suite policy gateway ref before admission.
The app envelope refuses ManualSsh routing and carries OpenTofu plan refs as metadata only; it does not execute commands or touch credentials.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: No deployed runtime path exists; rollup is O(n) over the supplied legal-entity snapshots and makes no I/O call.

findings.summary: Group rollup uses one Vec allocation sized to the legal entity input and no nested scans.

findings: Public fields carry data_class annotations and values are wrapped in Classified where stored in domain/app outputs.
The suite records evidence refs but does not claim durable audit-chain emission or compliance certification.
The change is additive: two crates, catalog rows, spec test refs, task rows, and evidence. No migration or persisted data path exists.
The app crate creates an audit-topic envelope for future adapters and records no runtime logs, metrics, or traces in this pure foundation slice.
Audit-chain JSONL rows record local evidence attachment and local Oya VCS lifecycle closeout.
Spec test refs were updated from earlier root-crate paths to flat microservice paths without deleting the pending AC-04/AC-05 future work.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: Enterprise Suite should be a policy and projection boundary, not a child-service implementation container.
M1_challenge_assumption.premise_evidence_ref: specs/microservices/enterprise-suite.json D-03 plus microservices/hr|payroll|accounting PRD non-suite boundaries
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: HR, Payroll, and Accounting foundations would remain individually valid but lack an implemented shared suite admission boundary.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: Waiting for REST/runtime adapters would mix pure policy invariants with deployment, storage, and Workflow concerns.

Validation is explicit and deterministic; group rollup uses linear projection over legal entity snapshots.
